acceptance.denominator: The bbg cycle records in the runner task's own --state-dir: 9 .cycle.json files, of which TWO have started_at at or after the 2026-10-13T05:52:43Z cut (20261013T055243Z and 20261013T080909Z) and both have ended. The script takes the FIRST ended record that HOLDS a failure, which is 20261013T080909Z: started_at 08:09:09Z, ended_at 17:37:08Z, completed False, stopped bot_check, failures 1. THE ONE FAILURE NAMES ITS REASON IN THE bx-3 FORM: key security-0f3eb2ded85ad44b, status bot_check, detail 'ChallengeFailed: bot_check challenge_failed (bloomberg_press_and_hold)' -- that is '<ExceptionClassName>: <message>' at 70 characters, inside the 303-character cap, and NOT the bare word 'error' that every record before this pin carried. Measured rather than eyeballed: the detail contains ':', DIFFERS from status, and is non-empty, which are the three things the script counts as NAMED. So NAMED=1 of FAILED=1. A TRUNCATED RECORD IS ALLOWED TO SERVE THIS READ by the order's own words ('a truncated record that DOES hold a failure still serves the read'); nothing here claims the cycle was completed or failure-free -- completed is False and is recorded as False. REGEX CONTROLS, so the PASS is the record's and not the pattern's: the live line MATCHES; this cell's OWN previous reading 'CYCLE=20261013T055243Z STOPPED=stopped_by_operator FAILED=0 NAMED=0' does NOT match; 'FAILED=1 NAMED=0' does NOT match (it really tests NAMED == FAILED); 'FAILED=8 NAMED=8' does match. NOTHING WAS DRIVEN: no pair planted or re-queued, no sign-in, the task not stopped, started or re-registered, and the state dir never written -- the failure is the runner's own, from its own cycle, read after the fact.

mutant.description: The order names no planted mutant and FORBIDS one by name ('do NOT plant a failure, re-queue a pair or touch the state dir to make the read pass'). The discriminating negative arm is this cell's own earlier reading, taken twice before the close and left in the record: the truncated 055243Z record printed FAILED=0 NAMED=0, which AC1 rejects.
mutant.expected: A record with no failure, or a failure whose detail does not name a reason, must FAIL AC1; only an ended record holding at least one failure whose detail names its reason may pass.
mutant.observed: Read at 09:0xZ and again at 18:1xZ: FAILED=0 NAMED=0 on the truncated record, AC1 FAIL, recorded as FAIL and left to stand. Read a third time at 18:1xZ after the windowless cycle ended: FAILED=1 NAMED=1, AC1 MATCH. The transition came from the runner finishing its own cycle, not from any act of this seat. The round-79 record (8 failures, all bare 'error') is the issuer's own recorded negative arm for the same regex and prints FAILED=8 NAMED=0.

determinism.method: Read-only, and run three times across about nine hours against the live state dir. The script globs the state dir and writes nothing; the two earlier runs and this one used the identical literal invocation.
determinism.observed: STABLE at each point in time and the change between them is the world's, not the instrument's: the same command returned the same truncated record twice while no cycle had ended, then returned the newly ended 080909Z record once it had. The record copied for this close is byte-identical to its source (len=514, sha256 5e652eaf...), so what was graded is what the runner wrote.
